name: Iproniazid
summary: Iproniazid was one of the first antidepressants discovered. It was first developed for tuberculosis, and its mood-lifting effects led to its use as an antidepressant in the 1950s.
description: Iproniazid was one of the first antidepressants discovered, first developed for tuberculosis. It was found to lift mood, which led to its use as an antidepressant in the 1950s. As a non-selective, irreversible MAOI, it raises levels of serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine in the brain. Because of a high risk of liver damage, it has been withdrawn from most markets.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Iproniazid was one of the first antidepressants discovered, initially developed for tuberculosis. It was found to have mood-elevating properties, leading to its use as an antidepressant in the 1950s. As a non-selective, irreversible MAOI, it increases synaptic levels of serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine. Due to high hepatotoxicity risk, it has been withdrawn from most markets.
